identity.canonical_program_name: Georgian National Film Centre Production Incentive
identity.administering_authority: See source_provenance; not separately normalized where absent.

authoritative_rule_text: Film in Georgia is a 20% cash rebate on qualified expenditure incurred in Georgia, with a further 2%-5% cultural uplift after the base certificate. A Georgia-registered production entity applies; at least 50% of the production budget must be mobilized at application; the applicant contracts with Enterprise Georgia, completes the production, and submits an independent qualified-cost audit within one year of certification. The official programme page sets five one-point uplift criteria covering release/making-of, specified Georgian key personnel, Georgian cultural content, at least GEL50,000 Georgian post-production, and qualifying international distribution or festival recognition. Local-entity payment alone does not qualify non-Georgian expenditure.

identity.canonical_program_name: Turkey Cinema General Directorate Production Support
identity.administering_authority: See source_provenance; not separately normalized where absent.

authoritative_rule_text: Foreign Film Production Support is selective support of up to 30% of the accepted amount spent in Turkey. The foreign producer must contract with an eligible Turkish co-producer or service company, which applies; the Turkish applicant must satisfy the official recent-production/service track record. The project must score at least 50/100 on the qualification test, be commercially exhibited abroad, and meet current minimum Turkey expenditure of TRY30 million for a feature, TRY6 million for a documentary, or TRY10 million per series episode. For co-productions, eligible Turkey expenditure is apportioned by the foreign producer's ownership share. Payment is made once after completion on invoices and a sworn CPA report. The support cannot be combined with co-production support.

authoritative_rule_text: Telefilm's current official directory displays 57 country/territory headings, with the Belgium heading covering the Flemish, French and German-speaking Communities; Canadian Heritage reports 59 partner countries. Each pathway is governed by its own treaty/MOU. Telefilm requires a Canadian-controlled production company, preliminary recommendation normally at least 30 days before shooting (60 days for Hungary, Poland, Switzerland or Hong Kong), joint authority recognition, and arrangement-specific financial, creative, technical, nationality, format and territorial compliance. Contributions range from 15%-30% under the applicable treaty; participation and expenditure must be proportional. Treaty status gives national status, but CPTC and other incentives require separate applications and their remaining requirements.

economics.rate_basis: Treaty status is structural and does not itself create a rebate.
